questions.question: Why does lowering LDL-C reduce ASCVD risk?
choices: It eliminates all inflammation immediately
It reduces exposure to atherogenic particles that contribute to plaque formation over time
It treats every cause of chest pain
It directly raises cardiac output
questions.explanation: LDL-containing particles contribute to arterial-wall retention, inflammation, and plaque development; reducing exposure helps reduce ASCVD risk.

questions.question: Which best describes secondary prevention in lipid management?
choices: Preventing a first event in a patient without ASCVD
Risk reduction after established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
Treating only high triglycerides
Managing a medication allergy
questions.explanation: Secondary prevention applies after established ASCVD, such as prior MI, ischemic stroke, or symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.

questions.question: What is the central mechanism of statins?
choices: Increase intestinal sodium absorption
Inhibit HMG-CoA reductase and increase hepatic LDL-receptor activity
Block all platelet function
Directly dissolve atherosclerotic plaques
questions.explanation: Statins inhibit hepatic cholesterol synthesis through HMG-CoA reductase inhibition and increase LDL clearance through receptor activity.

questions.question: A patient reports muscle pain after a statin change. What is the best initial FNP approach?
choices: Assume permanent statin intolerance without assessment
Assess severity, timing, alternative causes, systemic symptoms, and possible interactions
Tell the patient muscle symptoms never matter
Add a second statin immediately
questions.explanation: Muscle symptoms require structured assessment; timing alone does not prove causality, and severe symptoms or dark urine need urgent evaluation.

questions.question: Which situation raises concern for familial hypercholesterolemia?
choices: A strong family history of premature ASCVD with very high LDL-C
One isolated normal lipid panel
A mild viral illness
A single missed medication dose
questions.explanation: Very high LDL-C plus premature ASCVD or a strong early family history should prompt consideration of inherited dyslipidemia and possible referral.

questions.question: Why is a full medication reconciliation important before or during statin therapy?
choices: Only supplements can change lipid response
Some medications can alter statin exposure and increase adverse-effect risk
Statins have no clinically relevant interactions
It replaces ASCVD risk assessment
questions.explanation: Some drugs affect statin metabolism or transport and can increase exposure; use a current interaction resource for decisions.

questions.question: What is an important distinction when evaluating elevated triglycerides?
choices: They never have a secondary cause
ASCVD-risk management and pancreatitis-risk assessment may require different urgency and plans
They are identical to LDL-C in every context
They do not relate to diabetes or alcohol exposure
questions.explanation: Triglyceride elevation has many secondary causes. Marked elevation can raise pancreatitis concern, whereas moderate elevation often prompts broader ASCVD-risk management.

questions.question: Which finding in a patient with markedly elevated triglycerides most warrants urgent evaluation?
choices: No symptoms and a request for nutrition advice
Acute severe epigastric pain with vomiting
A question about a future lipid panel
A preference for a different pharmacy
questions.explanation: Severe epigastric pain and vomiting with marked triglyceride elevation can indicate pancreatitis and require urgent evaluation.

questions.question: What is the appropriate role of nonstatin lipid-lowering therapy?
choices: It always replaces lifestyle and statin therapy
It may be considered for selected high-risk patients with inadequate response or statin intolerance
It is indicated for every mildly abnormal lipid panel
It removes the need to review adherence
questions.explanation: Nonstatin agents may be useful for selected patients, but indication, adherence, secondary causes, risk, access, and tolerability must be assessed.

questions.question: Which follow-up approach best reflects FNP-level lipid management?
choices: Focus on one lipid value and ignore symptoms
Assess response, adherence, adverse effects, interactions, affordability, and global cardiovascular risk
Stop all treatment if a patient has a question
Avoid discussing lifestyle once medication begins
questions.explanation: Effective lipid care combines medication response and safety with adherence support, lifestyle care, cost discussion, and management of all ASCVD risk factors.
